boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Free, under-21-safe art activities at FIU’s Patricia & Phillip Frost Art Museum.

cards.title: Browse the Frost Art Museum
cards.subtitle: Modesto A. Maidique Campus, 10975 SW 17th St
cards.notes: Plan a daytime gallery visit with friends, then take time with the exhibitions at your own pace. Check current museum hours before heading over.
cards.short_summary: Free public access to FIU’s on-campus art museum.
cards.evidence_claim: Frost Art Museum states that admission is always free and open to the public during normal museum hours.
cards.source_title: Visitor Information | Patricia & Phillip Frost Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday through Sunday, 11 a.m.–5 p.m.; closed Mondays and most legal and university holidays. Admission is free.

cards.title: Walk the Sculpture Park
cards.subtitle: Patricia & Phillip Frost Art Museum, MMC
cards.notes: Make this an easy outdoor art walk: follow the works around the museum grounds, pause for photos from public paths, and respect the installations.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor collection stop beside the Frost Art Museum.
cards.evidence_claim: Frost Art Museum offers tours of its outdoor Sculpture Park, and the museum states its programs are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Tours | Patricia & Phillip Frost Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Outdoor access is subject to campus conditions; no admission or purchase is required for the museum’s free public programming.

cards.title: Join a Tertulia Nights conversation
cards.subtitle: Patricia & Phillip Frost Art Museum, MMC
cards.notes: RSVP for this second-Thursday program, arrive ready to listen and discuss, and use the museum setting as a low-pressure cultural night out.
cards.short_summary: A monthly after-hours exchange with artists, scholars, and changemakers.
cards.evidence_claim: Frost Art Museum describes Tertulia Nights as a second-Thursday monthly program that is free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Community Programs | Patricia & Phillip Frost Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Recommended for ages 18 and older; RSVP through the museum’s current listing. The museum states the event is free and open to the public.

cards.title: See art at Frost After Dark
cards.subtitle: Patricia & Phillip Frost Art Museum, MMC
cards.notes: Choose a first Wednesday, reserve if requested, and use the extended evening opening to explore galleries with friends at a calmer pace.
cards.short_summary: A monthly evening opportunity to visit Frost’s galleries.
cards.evidence_claim: Frost Art Museum says Frost After Dark occurs on the first Wednesday each month and that admission is free.
cards.source_title: Community Programs | Patricia & Phillip Frost Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Recommended for ages 18 and older; check the next event listing for details. Admission is free, while refreshments are optional.

cards.title: Make art at a Frost Family Day
cards.subtitle: Patricia & Phillip Frost Art Museum, MMC
cards.notes: Bring younger siblings or family members, join the hands-on activities, and check the museum calendar for the next spring or fall date.
cards.short_summary: Seasonal hands-on art activities connected to museum exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: Frost Art Museum says Family Days take place every spring and fall and include hands-on art activities; museum programs are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Community Programs | Patricia & Phillip Frost Art Museum
cards.access_notes: All ages are welcome, though programming is geared to pre-K through middle-school ages. Check the museum calendar for the next date; no admission is required.

cards.title: Sketch during Drawing You In
cards.subtitle: Patricia & Phillip Frost Art Museum, MMC
cards.notes: Reserve a spot for the monthly drawing session, work through the gallery prompts, and bring a friend who wants a guided creative break.
cards.short_summary: A monthly drawing workshop paired with an exhibition tour.
cards.evidence_claim: Frost Art Museum describes Drawing You In as a monthly drawing session and exhibition tour, with all materials provided.
cards.source_title: Community Programs | Patricia & Phillip Frost Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Recommended for ages 14 and older; reserve through the museum’s current listing. Materials are provided and museum admission is always free.

cards.title: Book a guided gallery tour
cards.subtitle: Patricia & Phillip Frost Art Museum, MMC
cards.notes: Coordinate a group visit, submit the tour request at least three weeks ahead, and ask for an experience suited to your group’s interests.
cards.short_summary: A museum-led tour of current exhibitions and the Sculpture Park.
cards.evidence_claim: Frost Art Museum offers guided tours for FIU students and groups, non-FIU university groups, schools, and community organizations.
cards.source_title: Tours | Patricia & Phillip Frost Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Submit a request at least three weeks in advance. The museum states admission is always free; confirm group-tour availability when requesting.

cards.title: Take a self-guided museum tour
cards.subtitle: Patricia & Phillip Frost Art Museum, MMC
cards.notes: Pick an exhibition route together, move slowly through the galleries, and use the museum’s digital audio-tour content to compare observations afterward.
cards.short_summary: A flexible, independent way to explore Frost exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: Frost Art Museum invites visitors to experience a self-guided in-person audio tour through its museum app.
cards.source_title: Tours | Patricia & Phillip Frost Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Visit during normal museum hours. Frost states admission is always free and open to the public; use of the self-guided experience requires no purchase.

cards.title: Join FIU Museums Insiders
cards.subtitle: Patricia & Phillip Frost Art Museum, MMC
cards.notes: If you are currently enrolled, sign up for the student community, then use its museum connection as a reason to return with classmates.
cards.short_summary: A no-cost FIU student community for museum engagement.
cards.evidence_claim: Frost Art Museum states that currently enrolled FIU undergraduate and graduate students can join its FIU Museums Insiders program and that participation is 100% free.
cards.source_title: Patricia & Phillip Frost Art Museum FIU
cards.access_notes: For currently enrolled FIU undergraduate and graduate students. The museum states participation in the program is 100% free.

cards.entity_name: iWitness Lunch Break: Finding Sanctuary in the Diaspora
cards.title: Attend the iWitness Lunch Break
cards.subtitle: SIPA II Room 102, MMC • Aug. 28, 2026
cards.notes: Register for the discussion, arrive with time to settle in, and stay afterward to talk through the ideas with friends or classmates.
cards.short_summary: A public humanities program centered on diaspora, visual storytelling, and dialogue.
cards.evidence_claim: FIU lists this August 28, 2026 iWitness Lunch Break program as free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: iWitness Lunch Break Fall 2026: Finding Sanctuary in the Diaspora | FIU Calendar
cards.access_notes: Friday, August 28, 2026, noon–2 p.m.; registration is listed by FIU. The event is free and open to the public.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented FIU study environments spanning its libraries, student centers, academic support spaces, and outdoor seating.

cards.title: Steven and Dorothea Green Library
cards.subtitle: Modesto A. Maidique Campus
cards.notes: Choose a quiet zone, computer lab, or reservable group room according to the kind of work you need to finish.
cards.short_summary: FIU’s main library offers seating, quiet zones, computer labs, and group-study rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: FIU Student Affairs identifies Green Library as a study location with seating, quiet zones, computer labs, and group study rooms.
cards.access_notes: Bring your FIU One Card; FIU Libraries says it is needed to enter Green Library and for study-room reservations.

cards.title: Glenn Hubert Library
cards.subtitle: Biscayne Bay Campus, North Miami Beach
cards.notes: Use the quiet zones for independent reading, or select a computer lab or group room when your assignment needs tools or collaborators.
cards.short_summary: The Biscayne Bay library combines library seating with quiet, computer, and group-study options.
cards.evidence_claim: FIU Student Affairs identifies Hubert Library as a study location with seating, quiet zones, computer labs, and group study rooms.
cards.access_notes: Located at FIU’s Biscayne Bay Campus; confirm library hours and room availability before traveling.

cards.title: FIU@I-75 Reserved Study Spaces
cards.subtitle: FIU@I-75, Miramar
cards.notes: Reserve a study space before heading to the I-75 site, especially if you need a dedicated room rather than open computer-lab seating.
cards.short_summary: A reservable study-space option at FIU’s I-75 location.
cards.evidence_claim: FIU Student Affairs states that FIU@75 offers reserved study spaces in addition to computer labs.
cards.access_notes: Reservation is required for the designated study spaces; verify availability through FIU’s study-space reservation service.

cards.title: Deuxieme Maison Sky Lounge
cards.subtitle: Modesto A. Maidique Campus
cards.notes: Bring a charged device and work outdoors in the converted courtyard; it is suited to reading or laptop tasks that tolerate an alfresco setting.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor courtyard study setting at Deuxieme Maison.
cards.evidence_claim: FIU Student Affairs describes the Sky Lounge as an alfresco study space created from a neglected Deuxieme Maison courtyard.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor setting; plan around weather and use normal campus-access rules.

cards.title: Academic Resource Center
cards.subtitle: Modesto A. Maidique Campus residential area
cards.notes: Pair a focused study session with an academic-success workshop, tutoring, or undergraduate advising if you need structured help.
cards.short_summary: A residential-student academic support hub with study space and learning services.
cards.evidence_claim: FIU Student Affairs states that the Academic Resource Center provides residential students study spaces, workshops, tutors, and undergraduate advising.
cards.access_notes: Study-space access is for residential students; academic-support services have their own availability and appointment requirements.

cards.title: Student-Athlete Academic Center
cards.subtitle: Modesto A. Maidique Campus
cards.notes: Use the center’s study space or computer lab alongside tutoring and meetings with Academic Coordinators when you are an eligible student-athlete.
cards.short_summary: Academic-support hub with study space and computer labs for FIU student-athletes.
cards.evidence_claim: FIU’s Student-Athlete Academic Center lists study spaces, computer labs, tutoring, and Academic Coordinator meetings among its resources.
cards.access_notes: Designed for FIU student-athletes; the official page lists weekday operating hours, which may change during breaks.

cards.entity_name: Graham Center Second-Floor Classroom Wing Lounge
cards.title: Graham Center Second-Floor Classroom Wing Lounge
cards.subtitle: Graham Center, Modesto A. Maidique Campus
cards.notes: Set up in the second-floor lounge when you want a shared academic setting that supports either solo work or a small group session.
cards.short_summary: A large Graham Center lounge explicitly suited to individual and group work.
cards.evidence_claim: FIU’s graduate catalog describes the Graham Center’s second-floor classroom wing as having a large lounge ideal for individual study and group work.
cards.access_notes: Located inside the Graham Center classroom wing; use it during building access hours and yield space for scheduled activity.

cards.title: FIU Law Library
cards.subtitle: Rafael Diaz-Balart Hall, Modesto A. Maidique Campus
cards.notes: Select an individual desk for focused reading, reserve a private room when eligible, or use collaborative space for a project with classmates.
cards.short_summary: A three-floor law library with private, individual, computer, and collaborative study settings.
cards.evidence_claim: FIU Law Library lists private study rooms, individual desks, computer workstations, and collaborative spaces among its study environments.
cards.access_notes: Anyone conducting legal research is welcome; after-hours access is limited to enrolled law students and recent law alumni studying for the bar.

cards.title: LACIC Quiet Study Room GL225A
cards.subtitle: Green Library, Modesto A. Maidique Campus
cards.notes: Use the quiet room for concentrated work, then draw on the nearby Latin American and Caribbean reference materials and research support.
cards.short_summary: A named quiet-study room within FIU’s Latin American and Caribbean Information Center.
cards.evidence_claim: FIU’s Latin American and Caribbean Information Center lists Quiet Study Room GL225A within its Green Library information area.
cards.access_notes: The LACIC Information Area lists weekday hours of 9 a.m.–6 p.m.; confirm current hours and room availability before visiting.

cards.title: Digital Scholar Studio GL 540
cards.subtitle: Green Library, Modesto A. Maidique Campus
cards.notes: Book an appointment when your project needs digital-scholarship workspace, training, or help with publishing, mapping, digitization, or oral history.
cards.short_summary: Appointment-based digital scholarship workspace in Green Library.
cards.evidence_claim: FIU Libraries describes the Digital Scholar Studio as providing tools, training, and workspace in digital scholarship at GL 540.
cards.access_notes: GL 540 is open by appointment; contact the Digital Scholar Studio before visiting.

warnings: The Graham Center source is FIU’s 2023–2024 graduate catalog; confirm building access conditions on the day of use.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Named Sweetwater destinations beside FIU’s Modesto A. Maidique Campus, organized around the SW 107th–117th Avenue and SW 2nd–7th Street corridors.

cards.title: Carlow Park
cards.subtitle: SW 5th Street corridor, by SW 106th Avenue
cards.notes: Bring a racquet or ball and use the listed pickleball courts, basketball court, or playground; the city also notes gazebos on site.
cards.short_summary: A city park with courts, a playground, and reservable gazebos.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Sweetwater lists Carlow Park at SW 106 Avenue and SW 4 Street with 10 pickleball courts, a basketball court, playground, and gazebos.
cards.access_notes: City page identifies the park and its amenities; check the city for reservation details.

cards.title: James M. Beasley Linear Park
cards.subtitle: Tamiami Canal corridor, SW 107th–117th Avenues
cards.notes: Use the one-mile bike path or vita course for a moving study break, then pause at a bench or covered rest station.
cards.short_summary: A canal-side linear park with a bike path and fitness course.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Sweetwater says James M. Beasley Linear Park runs along the Tamiami Canal between SW 107 and SW 117 Avenues and offers a bike path and vita course.
cards.source_title: James M. Beasley Linear Park | Sweetwater, FL
cards.access_notes: The city describes benches, lighting, water fountains, and two shelter rest stations along the park.

cards.title: Jose “Lolo” Villalobos Dominoes Park
cards.subtitle: SW 7th Terrace corridor, near SW 106th Avenue
cards.notes: Plan a daytime pause under the gazebo and bring a domino set; the city identifies sheltered domino tables, a tot lot, and restrooms.
cards.short_summary: A small public park built around sheltered domino tables.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Sweetwater lists Jose “Lolo” Villalobos Dominoes Park at 10620 SW 7th Terrace and describes a gazebo, sheltered domino tables, tot lot, bathrooms, and parking.
cards.source_title: Jose “Lolo” Villalobos Dominoes Park | Sweetwater, FL
cards.access_notes: The city states that the park is open to the public from sunrise to sunset.

cards.title: Ronselli Park
cards.subtitle: SW 114th Avenue corridor, at SW 2nd Street
cards.notes: Choose a field or court session before heading back: the city lists baseball, basketball, pickleball, soccer, football, and a playground.
cards.short_summary: Sweetwater’s largest park with several fields, courts, and a playground.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Sweetwater identifies Ronselli Park at SW 114 Avenue and SW 2 Street and lists baseball, basketball, pickleball, soccer, football, and playground facilities.
cards.access_notes: The city lists fields, courts, and the playground as open to the public daily from 8 AM to 9 PM.

cards.title: Jorge Mas Canosa Youth Center
cards.subtitle: SW 114th Avenue corridor, inside Ronselli Park
cards.notes: Check the city calendar before visiting; the center is the documented site for youth arts, music, dance, karate, camps, and civic events.
cards.short_summary: A named Ronselli Park center used for youth programs and events.
cards.evidence_claim: Sweetwater identifies the Jorge Mas Canosa Youth Center within Ronselli Park and describes ballet, music, Latin dance, karate, camps, and special events there.
cards.access_notes: Program availability and registration vary; consult the City of Sweetwater calendar or Parks and Recreation office.

cards.title: City of Sweetwater Community Center
cards.subtitle: SW 4th Street corridor, at SW 106th Avenue
cards.notes: Look at the center’s current programming before making the short trip; its stated focus is complimentary services and activities for senior residents.
cards.short_summary: A city community center serving senior residents with programs and services.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Sweetwater lists its Community Center at 10600 SW 4th Street and says it offers complimentary programs and services for senior residents on weekdays.
cards.source_title: City of Sweetwater Community Center | Sweetwater, FL
cards.access_notes: The city says the center is open Monday through Friday; its listed programming is aimed at senior residents.

cards.title: Sweetwater City Hall
cards.subtitle: SW 109th Avenue corridor, at SW 5th Street
cards.notes: Use the municipal hub when you need a documented local-government stop; confirm the appropriate department or service before you go.
cards.short_summary: Sweetwater’s named municipal hub and contact point.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Sweetwater lists Sweetwater City Hall at 500 SW 109 Avenue, Sweetwater, FL 33174.
cards.access_notes: Contact the city to confirm department availability and service requirements before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Sweetwater Historic Bridge and Surrounding Plaza
cards.title: Sweetwater Historic Bridge and Surrounding Plaza
cards.subtitle: SW 7th Terrace corridor, immediately east of SW 109th Avenue
cards.notes: Walk this documented civic restoration site as part of a SW 7th Terrace loop, and look for the added seating, lighting, and preserved bridge character.
cards.short_summary: A named historic-bridge plaza restoration location on SW 7th Terrace.
cards.evidence_claim: Sweetwater’s annual report locates the Historic Bridge and Surrounding Plaza restoration at SW 7th Terrace immediately east of SW 109th Avenue.
cards.access_notes: The cited report documents a restoration project; verify current on-site conditions before a visit.

cards.entity_name: Brothers to the Rescue Memorial Plaza
cards.title: Brothers to the Rescue Memorial Plaza
cards.subtitle: SW 7th Terrace corridor, west of SW 109th Avenue
cards.notes: Add the memorial plaza to a linear-park walk and take time to read the public-facing plaques or signage that are part of the documented plaza plan.
cards.short_summary: A named memorial-plaza destination beside the linear park corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: FIU’s UniversityCity traffic-study plan identifies an expansion of Brothers to the Rescue Memorial Plaza west of SW 109th Avenue beside the linear park.
cards.access_notes: The FIU planning document describes the plaza and linear-park improvements; confirm current access on arrival.

cards.title: FIU Engineering Center
cards.subtitle: West Flagler Street corridor, north of MMC
cards.notes: Use FIU’s campus map to locate this separate university destination and orient yourself before travel; it is listed alongside MMC and Biscayne Bay Campus maps.
cards.short_summary: FIU’s named Engineering Center location off the main MMC footprint.
cards.evidence_claim: FIU Campus Maps provides a distinct Engineering Center map in addition to its Modesto Maidique Campus and Biscayne Bay Campus maps.
cards.access_notes: Use FIU’s interactive map for the current building location, directions, and access information.
